comments:
Test looks racy - its possible for this to happen if the test thread is delayed a long time. However, running it constantly for half an hour didn't reproduce it.

The test could be rewritten to use `CyclicBarrier` in some form - lets see if it happens again soon before rewriting.

review_comments:
This is clever, but it required me a bit too much to understand why 2 and how it interacts with the `for(i.. iteration) barrier.await()`. 
I see the point of using basic primitives in this kind of tests, to be as much as possible in control and depend on as little as possible, but I wonder if using `CompletableFuture` here could bring an advantage in readability.
I'm not sure how CompetableFuture could be used here

You are right, I was thinking about having `countingRunnable` complete futures from an array and then `CompletableFuture.allOf(c).whenComplete((unused, throwable) -> cancellable.get().cancel());`, but reading the docs there is no guarantee that the continuation will run on the completing thread (it might, but it's not certain), opening the door for "unwanted" interleaving (all iterations complete before setting cancellable, "another round" of counting to go, etc.). While the CyclicBarrier action is " performed by the last thread entering the barrier."
